_comment: graft-uptake nudge config for the GJC pre_tool_use discovery hooks.
Surfaces: search / search_tool_bm25 / find / read, plus grep-like bash.
Merge order: built-in defaults <- ~/.gjc/agent/hooks/graft-nudge.json (user)
<- <project>/.gjc/graft-nudge.json (project). Later wins.
Default enabled=true: this harness drives graft uptake globally, so sync_gjc_hooks
seeds this as ~/.gjc/agent/hooks/graft-nudge.json (only if absent — your enabled choice
is never overwritten). It stays a NO-OP in any repo without a built graft/ graph.
To disable globally: set enabled=false here (or in ~/.gjc/agent/hooks/graft-nudge.json).
To pilot/override one repo: put { "enabled": true|false } in <project>/.gjc/graft-nudge.json.
What it does: when a repo has a built graft/ code-graph and the model reaches
for a discovery tool (search / search_tool_bm25 / find / whole-file read) or a
raw grep/rg bash scan BEFORE using graft this session, the hook runs
`graft ask <query> --json -n <results>` and returns the top pointers as the
block reason, steering the model into the graph. block-until-graft: the FIRST
`graft …` bash call flips the session state and unblocks every surface (so the
attitude-gate spec read and graft pointer reads are always reachable). A `graft`
command and mutating bash are never gated. maxNudges bounds total blocks.
Fields:
enabled      - master switch (default false).
maxNudges    - max blocks per session before yielding (deadlock guard).
askTimeoutMs - upper bound on the `graft ask` child, in ms.
results      - how many pointers to surface (graft ask -n).
